Download PRISM data

Source: R/source-prism.R
download_prism.Rd

Download one time period and climate element from the PRISM Climate Group Web Service. ZIP archives and extracted data are stored in separate subdirectories using the shared download workflow.

Usage

download_prism(
  time,
  element = c("ppt", "tmin", "tmax", "tmean", "tdmean", "vpdmin", "vpdmax", "solslope",
    "soltotal", "solclear", "soltrans"),
  data_type = c("ts", "normals_800", "normals"),
  format = c("nc", "asc", "grib2"),
  directory_to_save = NULL,
  acknowledgement = FALSE,
  download = TRUE,
  remove_command = FALSE,
  unzip = TRUE,
  remove_zip = FALSE,
  hash = FALSE,
  show_progress = TRUE,
  max_tries = 20,
  rate_limit = 2
)

Arguments

time

character(1). Single time-period code, retaining leading zeros. For data_type = "ts", use YYYYMMDD for a daily grid (from 1981), YYYYMM for a monthly grid (from 1895), or YYYY for an annual grid (from 1895). Each time-series request selects one grid. The legacy normals options use MM for a monthly normal, "14" for an annual normal, or MMDD for a daily normal; see Details for service availability. Local validation requires a character scalar with 2, 4, 6, or 8 characters; it does not validate calendar dates or availability.

element

character(1). Climate element: "ppt" (default), "tmin", "tmax", "tmean", "tdmean", "vpdmin", or "vpdmax". The legacy normals options also accept "solslope", "soltotal", "solclear", and "soltrans"; these are rejected for "ts".

data_type

character(1). Selected data type: "ts" (default) for 4 km time series, "normals_800" for the legacy 800 m normals URL template, or "normals" for the legacy 4 km normals URL template. See Details for service availability.

format

character(1). Requested time-series raster format: "nc" (default), "asc", or "grib2". The argument is validated but omitted from normals requests, with a message. See Details for provider support.

directory_to_save

character(1). Non-empty parent directory. Archives are downloaded into zip_files/ and, when unzip = TRUE, extracted into data_files/.

acknowledgement

logical(1). Must be TRUE to proceed. Downloaded archives and extracted rasters can require substantial storage.

download

logical(1). Deprecated. FALSE warns and returns a preview after directory creation, without contacting the service, downloading, or validating archives. Default is TRUE.

remove_command

logical(1). Deprecated and ignored; TRUE warns. No command file is generated. Default is FALSE.

unzip

logical(1). Extract the validated ZIP archive into data_files/. Default is TRUE. FALSE retains the archive without extracting it; ZIP validation still runs when download = TRUE.

remove_zip

logical(1). Remove the downloaded archive and its zip_files/ directory, including remaining contents, after extraction. Default is FALSE. May be TRUE only when unzip = TRUE. No removal occurs when download = FALSE.

hash

logical(1). Return a combined MD5 hash of the files under data_files/ instead of the download summary. Default is FALSE. Ignored when download = FALSE.

show_progress

logical(1). Show file download progress. Default is TRUE. Other status messages may still be printed when FALSE.

max_tries

integer(1). Maximum attempts per file download request, including the initial attempt. Default is 20.

rate_limit

numeric(1). Non-negative throttling interval in seconds, passed to download_run_method(). Default is 2.

Value

With download = FALSE, an invisible preview list containing urls, destfiles, and n_files. Otherwise, after downloading, validation, and optional extraction, hash = FALSE returns the download summary from download_run_method() invisibly. With hash = TRUE, returns a visible character scalar containing the combined MD5 hash of data_files/.

The download summary always contains success, failed, skipped, failed_urls, and failed_files. The two failure vectors are character(0) when no files failed, including when every file was skipped.

Details

zip_files/ and data_files/ are sibling directories created beneath directory_to_save, including for previews and when unzip = FALSE. The local archive name is constructed from the requested element, data type, time, and, for time series, format. Names and paths inside the archive are preserved during extraction.

After downloading, the destination archive is checked by listing its contents with utils::unzip(). This check also applies to existing non-empty archives skipped by download_run_method(). An unreadable ZIP raises an error, with a preview of the response text when available. Listing an archive does not fully verify its members or raster contents.

Hashing covers all files under data_files/, including existing files, and excludes archives in zip_files/. With unzip = FALSE, hashing still uses data_files/, which may be empty or contain previously extracted data.

The PRISM Web Service Guide dated 26 March 2025 documents time-series ZIP downloads, with daily data from 1981 and monthly and annual data from 1895. It states that normals are unavailable through this service and lists nc, asc, and bil format conversions, rather than grib2. The normals and grib2 options remain accepted by this function but are not documented as supported by the current service. See the guide in References.

References

Daly C, Taylor GH, Gibson WP, Parzybok TW, Johnson GL, Pasteris PA (2000). “HIGH-QUALITY SPATIAL CLIMATE DATA SETS FOR THE UNITED STATES AND BEYOND.” Transactions of the ASAE, 43(6), 1957–1962. ISSN 2151-0059. doi:10.13031/2013.3101 . http://elibrary.asabe.org/abstract.asp??JID=3&AID=3101&CID=t2000&v=43&i=6&T=1.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
download_prism(
  time = "202104",
  element = "ppt",
  data_type = "ts",
  format = "nc",
  directory_to_save = file.path(tempdir(), "prism"),
  acknowledgement = TRUE,
  download = FALSE # Preview the URL and zip_files/ destination.
)
} # }
